prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1155; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer narrative. On arrival at the intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, I observed a side impact between two vehicles. Driver 1 was operating the vehicle that struck the passenger side of Driver 2's vehicle as Driver 2 proceeded through on a green signal. Driver 1 confirmed that the vehicle he was operating is insured under a policy in his name. Driver 2 reported a wrist injury, which I noted at the scene. Passenger was seated in the front of Driver 2's vehicle and was identified by both drivers and by two independent witnesses, who stated they saw the collision and the position of both vehicles before they came to rest. Scene photographs were taken and show damage concentrated on the impacted side of each vehicle, consistent with the reported angle and force of the collision. Driver 1 stated that the vehicle had no prior damage to the area involved, and nothing observed at the scene contradicted this. Both vehicles were towed from the scene. A citation was issued to Driver 1 for failure to yield the right of way.
